How much more, in dollars, did a ton of river rock cost Odalys than a cubic yard of mulch? Enter decimal form only.
questions.explanation: The coefficients are the unit prices: 29.75 − 19.5 = 10.25.

questions.question:
9x + y = 22
10x − y = 16
How many solutions does the given system of equations have?
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives 19x = 38, so x = 2 and y = 4. The lines have different slopes (−9 and 10), so there is exactly one solution.

questions.question:
y = 5x
y = 2x + 2
How many solutions does the given system of equations have?
questions.explanation: The slopes 5 and 2 differ, so the lines intersect at exactly one point (5x = 2x + 2 gives x = 2/3).

questions.question: The equation y = −4.9(x − 9.1)2 + 10,700 gives the estimated height above ground, y, in meters, of a plane, where x is the number of seconds since it started a parabolic maneuver. If this equation is graphed in the xy−plane, which of the following is the best interpretation of the vertex of the graph?
options: The plane reached an estimated maximum height of 10,700 meters 4.9 seconds after it started the parabolic maneuver.
The plane reached an estimated maximum height of 10,700 meters 9.1 seconds after it started the parabolic maneuver.
The plane reached an estimated maximum height of 4.9 meters 10,700 seconds after it started the parabolic maneuver.
The plane reached an estimated maximum height of 9.1 meters 10,700 seconds after it started the parabolic maneuver.
questions.explanation: The vertex is (9.1, 10,700): a maximum height of 10,700 meters at 9.1 seconds.

questions.question:
x2 + y2 = 1,088
y − 4x = 0
A solution to the given system of equations is (x, y), where x < 0. What is the value of y?
questions.explanation: Substituting y = 4x gives 17x^2 = 1,088, so x^2 = 64 and x = −8 (since x < 0). Then y = 4(−8) = −32.

questions.question: y = 9((a)/(7))(x+c) − b. How many times does the graph of the given equation in the xy−plane cross the x−axis, where a, b, and c are positive constants such that a > 7 and b > c?
questions.explanation: Since a/7 > 1 the function is an increasing exponential with range y > −b, and −b < 0, so it takes the value 0 exactly once.

options: The measures of angle B and angle R are 34° and 94°, respectively.
The measures of angle B and angle Q are 52° and 34°, respectively.
questions.explanation: With B = 34°, angle C = 180 − 52 − 34 = 94°. With P = 52° and R = 94°, angle Q = 34°, so all three angles match and the triangles are similar by AA.

questions.question: In right triangle RST, the sum of the measures of angle R and angle S is 90 degrees. The value of sin(R) is 3√1713. What is the value of cos(S)?
questions.explanation: R and S are complementary, so cos(S) = sin(R) = (3√17)/13.

questions.question:
nx2 − 16x = 26x2 − 8
In the given equation, n is an integer constant. If the equation has two distinct real solutions, what is the greatest possible value of n?
questions.explanation: Rewrite as (n − 26)x^2 − 16x + 8 = 0. The discriminant 256 − 32(n − 26) must be positive, so n < 34 and the greatest integer is 33.

questions.question: Jasmin grows bean pods in her garden. This year, she harvested 330 bean pods and saved 10% of them to plant next year. How many of the harvested bean pods did Jasmin save to plant next year?

An environmental scientist is investigating the volatility of 175 organic compounds by finding the boiling point of each compound. The mean boiling point of all 175 compounds is 183 degrees Celsius. The scientist classifies each of these compounds as either semivolatile or volatile. Of the 175 compounds, 50 compounds were classified as semivolatile, and these 50 compounds have a mean boiling point of 338 degrees Celsius. The remaining 125 compounds were classified as volatile. What is the mean boiling point, in degrees Celsius, of the 125 compounds classified as volatile?
questions.explanation: Total = 175(183) = 32,025; semivolatile total = 50(338) = 16,900; so the volatile mean is 15,125/125 = 121.

questions.question: The equation N(m) = 61(Q)<sup>m/4</sup> gives the predicted population N(m), in thousands, of a certain bacteria colony m minutes after the initial measurement, where Q is a constant greater than 1. The predicted population increases by p% every 120 seconds. What is the value of p in terms of Q?
questions.explanation: 120 seconds is 2 minutes, so the population is multiplied by Q^(2/4) = Q^(1/2). The percent increase is 100(Q^(1/2) − 1).

questions.question: The kinetic energy K, in joules, of an object is given by the formula K = 12mv2, where m is the mass of the object, in kilograms, and v is the velocity of the object, in meters per second. If the kinetic energy of a certain object can be found by using the formula K = 32v2, what is the mass of the object, in kilograms?
A triangle has a base length of 48 centimeters and a height of 96 centimeters. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the triangle?
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2)(48)(96) = 2,304 square centimeters.

questions.question:
x2 − 4x + y2 − 8y − 80 = 0
In the xy−plane, the graph of the given equation is a circle. If this circle is inscribed in a square, what is the perimeter of the square?
questions.explanation: Completing the square gives (x − 2)^2 + (y − 4)^2 = 100, so r = 10. The square has side 20 and perimeter 80.

questions.question: For triangle ABC, the length of AB is 11 less than the length of AC. Point D (not shown) lies on AC such that BD (not shown) is perpendicular to AC. What is the value of BCBD?
questions.explanation: AB = 28 − 11 = 17. In right triangle BCD, sin C = BD/BC, and in triangle ABC, sin C = AB/AC = 17/28. So BC/BD = 28/17.

questions.question: The length of the diagonal of a square is 186√22 units. What is the area, in square units, of the square?
questions.explanation: Diagonal = s√2, so s = 186/2 = 93 and the area is 93² = 8,649.

questions.question: A conservation specialist hung artificial nesting structures, each in the shape of a right rectangular prism, for a species of native owl. Each structure has a height of 11 inches. The length of each structure’s base is x inches, which is 1 inch more than the width of the structure’s base. Which function V gives the volume of each structure, in cubic inches, in terms of the length of the structure’s base?
questions.explanation: Width = x − 1, height 11, so V = 11·x·(x − 1).
